303A.3 / CHAPTER 3 OF 11

Scout, then earn promotion

What new evidence would justify more exposure?

11 short chapters

01Choose the container02Opportunity vs portfolio risk03Scout, then earn promotion04Adding up or down05Harvest & residual exposure06Reset the mission07Break the attachment08Attention & holding time09Match the evidence to the market10Portfolio limits & concentration11Measure the net result

01Definition

A scout is limited initial exposure within a plan. Promotion means considering more exposure after independent evidence improves.

02Why it matters

Price movement alone does not answer whether the case or execution conditions improved.

03What to check

  • Current hygiene and unresolved critical evidence
  • Independent demand and thesis confirmation
  • Total exposure and executable cost after an add

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

A proposed add has fresh evidence and fits the original limits.

Dangerous

Excitement or fear of missing out drives promotion.

05Beginner mistake

Buying a position to replace the necessary due diligence.

06Takeaway

Promotion needs evidence, not just a moving price.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Price rises after a limited initial entry.

  2. 02

    Independent buyers and liquidity improve, while hygiene is rechecked.

  3. 03

    Consider the new evidence alongside the remaining budget.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Inspect

Compare sampled buyer activity and selling. Verify current hygiene, broader thesis evidence, and execution quotes separately.

Go deeper

Market confirmation can include persistent buyers, absorption, and liquidity changes. Thesis confirmation can include credible attention, a verified catalyst, or product evidence. Correlated copies of the same claim are not independent confirmation. Small size cannot fix a failed hygiene gate or guarantee an easy exit.
